text_blocks.snippet: Losartan is a prescription medication used to treat high blood pressure and protect kidney function, and its common side effects include dizziness, fatigue, and mild stomach upset.
snippet_highlighted_words: dizziness, fatigue, and mild stomach upset

text_blocks.snippet: Most mild side effects improve over time as your body adjusts to the medication:

list.snippet: Dizziness or lightheadedness: Caused by lowered blood pressure, especially when standing up quickly.
Fatigue: Feeling more tired than usual while your body adapts.
Nasal congestion: A stuffy nose or cold-like symptoms.
Headaches: Mild head pain or discomfort.
Digestive issues: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or stomach pain.
Aches: Back pain or joint pain.

text_blocks.snippet: Though rare, serious complications can occur:

list.snippet: High potassium (hyperkalemia): Can cause muscle weakness or irregular heartbeat, which is why doctors order routine blood tests.
Kidney function changes: Worsening kidney injury or decreased urination.
Severe low blood pressure: Extreme lightheadedness or fainting.
Angioedema: A dangerous allergic reaction causing swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat and trouble breathing.

text_blocks.snippet: You can read more comprehensive details on the Mayo Clinic guide or the MedlinePlus drug information page. You can also review patient guidance provided by the NHS.
